questions.question: Which logical operator outputs true only when both inputs are true?
questions.explanation: AND requires both operands to be true.

questions.question: Which logical operator inverts the truth value of its operand?
questions.explanation: NOT negates the input value.

questions.question: Which operator is true when at least one input is true?
questions.explanation: OR returns true if any operand is true.

questions.question: Which operator is true when exactly one input is true?
questions.explanation: XOR (exclusive OR) requires one true, one false.

questions.question: What does the NAND operator produce?
options: True if both inputs are true
False if both inputs are true
True only when exactly one input is true
False if one input is false
questions.explanation: NAND is NOT AND, false only when both true.

questions.question: What does the NOR operator produce?
options: True if both inputs are false
False if both inputs are false
True only when exactly one input is true
False if one input is true
questions.explanation: NOR is NOT OR, true only when both false.

questions.question: Which operator has the highest precedence in logic?
questions.explanation: NOT has highest precedence, evaluated first.

questions.question: What symbol represents the implication operator?
questions.explanation: → denotes logical implication (if-then).

questions.question: Which operator is commutative?
questions.explanation: OR is commutative: p∨q = q∨p.

questions.question: What is true for the biconditional operator?
questions.explanation: Biconditional is true when inputs have same value.

questions.question: Which logical operator is represented by the symbol ⊕?
questions.explanation: ⊕ denotes exclusive OR, true when exactly one operand is true.

questions.question: Which of the following is a unary operator?
questions.explanation: NOT operates on a single operand; the others are binary operators.

questions.question: How many rows of a two-input AND truth table contain True?
questions.explanation: AND is true only in the True-True row.

questions.question: How many rows of a two-input OR truth table contain True?
questions.explanation: OR is false only in the False-False row, so three rows are true.

questions.question: NAND is equivalent to which expression?
questions.explanation: NAND is the negation of conjunction: ¬(p∧q).

questions.question: NOR is equivalent to which expression?
questions.explanation: NOR is the negation of disjunction: ¬(p∨q).

questions.question: Which operator is NOT commutative?
questions.explanation: p→q is generally not equal to q→p; AND, OR, and XOR are commutative.

questions.question: What is p NAND p equivalent to?
questions.explanation: p NAND p = ¬(p∧p) = ¬p, which is how NAND gates build inverters.

questions.question: Which pair of operators is functionally complete?
questions.explanation: AND with NOT can express every Boolean function; the other pairs cannot express negation.

questions.question: The Sheffer stroke ↑ denotes which operator?
questions.explanation: The Sheffer stroke is an alternative notation for NAND.

questions.question: The Peirce arrow ↓ denotes which operator?
questions.explanation: The Peirce arrow (joint denial) is the symbol for NOR.

questions.question: Which operator is equivalent to ¬(p⊕q)?
questions.explanation: Negating XOR yields XNOR, which is exactly the biconditional p↔q.

questions.question: In the expression ¬p∨q∧r, which operation is evaluated first?
questions.explanation: Negation has the highest precedence, so ¬p is evaluated before ∧ and ∨.

questions.question: Which binary operator is associative?
questions.explanation: (p⊕q)⊕r ≡ p⊕(q⊕r); implication, NAND, and NOR are not associative.

questions.question: Which operator's output column contains exactly two True and two False rows?
questions.explanation: XOR is true in the True-False and False-True rows only — two of four rows.

questions.question: How many distinct Boolean operators (truth functions) on two variables exist?
questions.explanation: Each of the 4 input rows can map to True or False, giving 2^4 = 16 functions.

questions.question: A 2:1 multiplexer outputs (s∧a)∨(¬s∧b), selecting a when s=1 and b when s=0. With s=False, a=False, b=True, what is the output?
questions.explanation: s=F kills the s∧a term; ¬s∧b = T∧T = T, so the output follows b.

questions.question: Which expression computes p⊕q using only NAND gates?
options: (p NAND (p NAND q)) NAND (q NAND (p NAND q))
questions.explanation: Let t = p NAND q = ¬(p∧q). Then (p NAND t) = ¬p∨(p∧q) = ¬p∨q and (q NAND t) = ¬q∨p; NAND-ing them gives ¬((¬p∨q)∧(¬q∨p)) = (p∧¬q)∨(¬p∧q) = p⊕q.

questions.question: Evaluate (p⊕q)∧(p∨q) for p=True, q=False.
questions.explanation: T⊕F = T and T∨F = T, so T∧T = T.

questions.question: An alert rule fires when (alarm ∧ ¬maintenance) ⊕ override evaluates true. Given alarm=True, maintenance=True, override=True, does it fire?
options: Yes — alarm∧¬maintenance is False, and False⊕True = True
No — XOR requires both inputs true
questions.explanation: ¬maintenance = F makes the alarm term F; the override then flips it: F⊕T = T, so the rule fires.

questions.question: In how many of the four input rows is (p NOR q)→p true?
questions.explanation: The implication fails only when p NOR q is true and p is false: the row p=F, q=F. The other three rows are true.
